back: India accounts for approximately 24-25% of the world's total TB cases.
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 182 (Book Page): India alone accounts for 24 per cent of the world's TB cases.

category: Analyze the local and global burden of Tuberculosis
front: Q: How does malnutrition create a 'vicious loop' in Tuberculosis pathogenesis?
back: Malnutrition predisposes to active disease, worsens treatment outcomes, and facilitates spread by increasing viral excretion duration/intensity.
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 187 (Book Page): Malnutrition is widely believed to predispose to tuberculosis... it will continue to affect the development of active disease, outcome of treatment and spread.

category: Analyze the local and global burden of Tuberculosis
front: Q: What is the estimated global mortality rate for MDR-TB based on 2013 estimates?
back: Approximately 210,000 deaths annually.
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 182 (Book Page): it is estimated that about 1.5 million people died of TB... and 210,000 MDR-TB cases.

category: Analyze the local and global burden of Tuberculosis
front: Q: What proportion of the current global population is estimated to have asymptomatic Tuberculosis infection?
back: Approximately one-third (1/3) of the entire global population is infected asymptomatically.
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 182 (Book Page): [It is estimated that about one-third of the current global population is infected asymptomatically with tuberculosis]

category: Analyze the local and global burden of Tuberculosis
front: Q: How does HIV co-infection impact the global Tuberculosis mortality burden according to 2013 estimates?
back: Out of 1.5 million deaths, approximately 360,000 (24%) were HIV-positive individuals.
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 182 (Book Page): [It is estimated that about 1.5 million people died of TB, of these 360,000 were HIV positive]

category: Analyze the local and global burden of Tuberculosis
front: Q: Contrast the prevalence of MDR-TB in India between newly diagnosed and previously treated cases.
back:
- New cases: ~2.2%
- Retreatment cases: ~15%
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 183 (Book Page): [MDR-TB among notified new pulmonary TB patients was about 2.2 per cent, and among retreatment cases was about 15 per cent]

category: Analyze the local and global burden of Tuberculosis
front: Q: In a clinical setting, how many secondary infections can one infectious pulmonary TB patient cause annually?
back: An infectious patient typically infects between 10 to 15 persons per year.
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 182 (Book Page): [Patients with infectious pulmonary tuberculosis disease can infect 10-15 persons in a year.]

category: Analyze the local and global burden of Tuberculosis
front: Q: What is the primary epidemiological reason for the continued high childhood Tuberculosis mortality in developing countries?
back: Difficulty in diagnosis and the resulting lack of data on the actual pediatric burden.
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 182 (Book Page): [The actual burden of paediatric TB is not known due to diagnostic difficulties. It is assumed that about 10 per cent of total TB load is found in children.]

category: Analyze the local and global burden of Tuberculosis
front: Q: What was the Indian National ARTI (Annual Risk of TB Infection) based on the 2000-2003 survey?
back: The national ARTI was approximately 1.5 per cent.
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 183 (Book Page): [The survey showed the national ARTI was about 1.5 per cent.]

category: Analyze the local and global burden of Tuberculosis
front: Q: Explain the 'lethal combination' mentioned in the text that worsens the global Tuberculosis situation.
back: The combination of Tuberculosis and HIV is identified as a lethal alliance accelerating morbidity.
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 182 (Book Page): [To make global situation worse, tuberculosis has formed a lethal combination with HIV.]

category: Analyze the local and global burden of Tuberculosis
front: Q: Distinguish the Tuberculosis burden of India from the rest of the world by incident numbers.
back: India is the highest burden country, accounting for 24% (one-fourth) of global incident cases.
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 183 (Book Page): [India... accounts for one-fourth of the estimated global incident TB cases in 2013.]

category: Analyze the local and global burden of Tuberculosis
front: Q: What are the key non-medical 'social' determinants causing high Tuberculosis vulnerability in populations?
back:
- Poor quality of life/housing
- Overcrowding
- Malnutrition
- Smoking/Alcohol abuse
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 187 (Book Page): [The social factors include... poor housing, and overcrowding... undernutrition, smoking, alcohol abuse]

category: Analyze the local and global burden of Tuberculosis
front: Q: What is the long-term goal for global Tuberculosis incidence set for the year 2050?
back: To reach an incidence of less than or equal to 1 case per million population per year.
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 206 (Book Page): [By 2050: The global incidence of TB disease will be less than or equal to 1 case per million population per year.]

category: Analyze the local and global burden of Tuberculosis
front: What proportion of the global population is estimated to be asymptomatically infected with Tuberculosis?
back: Approximately one-third of the current global population is asymptomatically infected.
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 182 (Book Page): It is estimated that about one-third of the current global population is infected asymptomatically with tuberculosis, of whom 5-10 per cent will develop clinical disease during their lifetime.

category: Analyze the local and global burden of Tuberculosis
front: How many individuals can a single patient with infectious pulmonary tuberculosis infect annually?
back: An infectious patient can infect between 10 to 15 persons in a year.
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 182 (Book Page): Patients with infectious pulmonary tuberculosis disease can infect 10-15 persons in a year.

category: Analyze the local and global burden of Tuberculosis
front: Contrast the primary transmission source of Human vs. Bovine Tuberculosis strains.
back: Human strain: Droplet infection/nuclei from sputum-positive cases. Bovine strain: Ingestion of infected milk.
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 187 (Book Page): (i) Human source : The most common source of infection is the human case whose sputum is positive for tubercle bacilli... (ii) Bovine source: The bovine source of infection is usually infected milk.

category: Analyze the local and global burden of Tuberculosis
front: In a high-burden setting like India, what absolute proportion of the global TB incidence does the country account for?
back: India accounts for approximately 24% (one-fourth) of the world's total TB cases.
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 182 (Book Page): The South East Asia Region accounts for 39 per cent of the global burden of TB in terms of incidence and India alone accounts for 24 per cent of the world's TB cases.

category: Analyze the local and global burden of Tuberculosis
front: What is the primary objective of the 'Intensive Phase' in Tuberculosis chemotherapy?
back: To rapidly kill as many bacilli as possible to prevent the emergence of 'persisters' and reduce the risk of relapse.
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 193 (Book Page): During this intensive phase, three or more drugs are combined to kill off as many bacilli as possible. The more rapidly the bacilli are killed initially, the less likely are “persisters” to emerge.

category: Analyze the local and global burden of Tuberculosis
front: State the two specific global targets set for the DOTS programme regarding cure and detection.
back: 1. 85% cure rate of new smear-positive cases. 2. 70% detection rate of such cases.
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 183 (Book Page): The target of DOTS programme is successful treatment or cure rate of 85 per cent of new smear positive cases, and detection of 70 per cent of such cases.

category: Analyze the local and global burden of Tuberculosis
front: Why does BCG vaccination remain a priority in India despite varying protection rates?
back: It provides significant protection against severe childhood forms of TB, specifically tuberculous meningitis and miliary tuberculosis.
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 203 (Book Page): BCG administered early in life provides a high level of protection, particularly against the severe forms of childhood tuberculosis and tuberculous meningitis.

category: Analyze the local and global burden of Tuberculosis
front: What are the typical clinical causes of death in paediatric Tuberculosis cases?
back: Death in children usually results from tuberculous meningitis or disseminated (miliary) disease.
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 182 (Book Page): Childhood deaths from TB are usually caused by meningitis or disseminated disease.

category: Analyze the local and global burden of Tuberculosis
front: Describe the relationship between cell-mediated immunity and Tuberculosis pathogenesis.
back: TB resistance is cell-mediated; cellular immunity limits bacillary multiplication. Deficiency (e.g., HIV, malnutrition) facilitates progression to active disease.
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 187 (Book Page): It is now known that both delayed hypersensitivity and acquired resistance to tuberculosis are cell-mediated responses. In most cases, the cellular immunity proves adequate to limit further multiplication and spread of bacilli.

category: Analyze the local and global burden of Tuberculosis
front: What is the defining clinical tool for case-finding in Tuberculosis control programs?
back: Direct microscopic examination of sputum smear (Sputum examination).
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 188 (Book Page): Sputum smear examination by direct microscopy is now considered the method of choice. The reliability, cheapness and ease of direct microscopic examination has made it number one case-finding method all over the world.

category: Analyze the local and global burden of Tuberculosis
front: Q: What proportion of the global population is estimated to be asymptomatically infected with Tuberculosis?
back:
- Approximately one-third (33%) of the global population.
- 5-10% of these will develop clinical disease during their lifetime.
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 182 (Book Page): [It is estimated that about one-third of the current global population is infected asymptomatically with tuberculosis, of whom 5-10 per cent will develop clinical disease during their lifetime.]

category: Analyze the local and global burden of Tuberculosis
front: Q: What is the epidemiological significance of 'dormant' or 'persister' bacilli in TB relapses?
back:
- They are slow multipliers resistant to bactericidal action.
- They remain alive for years, acting as 'seeds' for future active disease (relapse) when host conditions favor them.
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 187 (Book Page): [The slow multipliers are the source of persister or dormant bacilli; they can remain alive for years without causing harm to the host, but... they are the seeds of a future relapse.]

category: Analyze the local and global burden of Tuberculosis
front: Q: Contrast the efficacy and target outcomes of DOTS vs. traditional self-administered therapy.
back:
- DOTS: Up to 95% treatment success; prevents MDR-TB emergence.
- Traditional: Higher default rates; relies on 18-month regimens; increases community resistance risk.
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 183 (Book Page): [The advantages of DOTS are... Treatment success rate is upto 95 per cent; Prevents failure of treatment and the emergence of MDR-TB by ensuring patient adherence.]

category: Analyze the local and global burden of Tuberculosis
front: Q: In a high-prevalence region, what is the statistical burden of TB/HIV co-infection on global mortality?
back:
- 13% of global TB cases are HIV-positive.
- Approximately 24% of TB-related deaths occur in HIV-positive patients.
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 182 (Book Page): [Of these incident cases 1.1 million (13 per cent) were HIV positives... It is estimated that about 1.5 million people died of TB, of these 360,000 were HIV positive.]

category: Analyze the local and global burden of Tuberculosis
front: Q: What is the primary pharmacologic goal of the 'intensive phase' (initial 2 months) of TB chemotherapy?
back:
- To kill rapidly multiplying bacilli immediately.
- To prevent the emergence of drug-resistant 'persisters' and reduce initial infectivity.
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 193 (Book Page): [During this intensive phase, three or more drugs are combined to kill off as many bacilli as possible. The more rapidly the bacilli are killed initially, the less likely are 'persisters' to emerge.]

category: Analyze the local and global burden of Tuberculosis
front: Q: What are the two specific performance targets set for a successful national DOTS program?
back:
- 85% cure rate (success) of new smear-positive cases.
- 70% detection rate of estimated new smear-positive cases.
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 183 (Book Page): [The target of DOTS programme is successful treatment or cure rate of 85 per cent of new smear positive cases, and detection of 70 per cent of such cases.]

category: Analyze the local and global burden of Tuberculosis
front: Q: How is the Annual Risk of TB Infection (ARTI) utilized to analyze local disease burden?
back:
- It estimates the percentage of the population infected/re-infected in one year.
- High-burden countries (like India/Pakistan) typically show an ARTI of 1.1% to 1.5%.
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 183 (Book Page): [The survey showed the national ARTI was about 1.5 per cent. The second survey (2009-2010) shows that the national ARTI is 1.1 per cent.]

category: Analyze the local and global burden of Tuberculosis
front: Q: Differentiate the primary transmission routes of Human vs. Bovine Tuberculosis strains.
back:
- Human strain: Droplet nuclei from sputum-positive patients.
- Bovine strain: Ingestion of infected milk (largely controlled by boiling locally).
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 187 (Book Page): [(i) Human source : The most common source of infection is the human case whose sputum is positive... (ii) Bovine source: The bovine source of infection is usually infected milk.]

category: Analyze the local and global burden of Tuberculosis
front: Q: Why does the protective value of BCG vary significantly (0-80%) in different global trials?
back:
- Environmental mycobacteria: Prior exposure to non-tuberculous species (e.g., M. vaccae) masks or antagonizes BCG benefit.
- Most effective when given before environmental exposure.
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 203 (Book Page): [prior exposure to some non-tuberculous environmental mycobacteria... may have conferred partial immunity on the population and thus masked the potential benefit of BCG.]

category: Analyze the local and global burden of Tuberculosis
front: Q: Which infectious material and conditions define the 'barometer of social welfare' in TB epidemiology?
back:
- Infectious material: Secretions/Sputum of smear-positive cases.
- Conditions: Overcrowding, poor housing, and malnutrition.
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 188 (Book Page): [Tuberculosis... has also been described as a barometer of social welfare... The social factors include... poor housing, and overcrowding, population explosion, undernutrition.]

category: Analyze the local and global burden of Tuberculosis
front: Q: What proportion of the current global population is estimated to be asymptomatically infected with Tuberculosis?
back:
- Approximately one-third of the global population.
- 5-10% of these will develop clinical disease in their lifetime.
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 182 (Book Page): [It is estimated that about one-third of the current global population is infected asymptomatically with tuberculosis, of whom 5-10 per cent will develop clinical disease during their lifetime.]

category: Analyze the local and global burden of Tuberculosis
front: Q: Describe the annual infectivity potential of a single untreated case of infectious pulmonary Tuberculosis.
back:
- One infectious case can infect 10-15 persons annually.
- This facilitates the rapid spread in high-burden, densely populated regions.
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 182 (Book Page): [Patients with infectious pulmonary tuberculosis disease can infect 10-15 persons in a year.]

category: Analyze the local and global burden of Tuberculosis
front: Q: Which WHO region bears the largest percentage of the global Tuberculosis incidence?
back:
- South East Asia Region (SEAR) accounts for 39% of the global burden.
- India alone accounts for 24% of worldwide cases.
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 182 (Book Page): [The South East Asia Region accounts for 39 per cent of the global burden of TB in terms of incidence and India alone accounts for 24 per cent of the world's TB cases.]

category: Analyze the local and global burden of Tuberculosis
front: Q: Based on 2013 global data, what is the prevalence of HIV co-infection among incident Tuberculosis cases?
back:
- Approximately 13% of incident cases (1.1 million people).
- TB is a leading cause of death in HIV-positive individuals.
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 182 (Book Page): [Of these incident cases 1.1 million (13 per cent) were HIV positives... 360,000 deaths were HIV positive.]

category: Analyze the local and global burden of Tuberculosis
front: Q: Contrast the prevalence of MDR-TB between new and previously treated Tuberculosis cases globally.
back:
- New cases: 3.5%.
- Previously treated cases: 20.5%.
- This indicates a significant burden of acquired resistance.
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 182 (Book Page): [3.5 per cent of the new and 20.5 per cent of previously treated cases were of MDR-TB.]

category: Analyze the local and global burden of Tuberculosis
front: Q: What is the current estimated global notification rate and volume of 'missed' Tuberculosis cases?
back:
- Notification rate: 64%.
- Missed cases: ~3 million cases either undiagnosed or not reported annually.
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 182 (Book Page): [The notification rate was about 64 per cent. About 3 million missed cases were either not diagnosed or diagnosed but not reported.]

category: Analyze the local and global burden of Tuberculosis
front: Q: Analyze the burden of paediatric Tuberculosis in terms of total caseload and yearly mortality.
back:
- 10% of total TB load (approx. 1 million cases/year).
- Results in over 100,000 deaths annually.
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 182 (Book Page): [It is assumed that about 10 per cent of total TB load is found in children. Globally, about 1 million cases of paediatric TB are estimated to occur every year, with more than 100,000 deaths.]

category: Analyze the local and global burden of Tuberculosis
front: Q: Identify the primary causes of Tuberculosis-related mortality in children.
back:
- Meningitis.
- Disseminated (miliary) disease.
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 182 (Book Page): [Childhood deaths from TB are usually caused by meningitis or disseminated disease.]

category: Analyze the local and global burden of Tuberculosis
front: Q: Define the Annual Risk of Tuberculosis Infection (ARTI) and its recent trends in India.
back:
- ARTI measures transmission within a community.
- Declined from 1.5% (2000-2003) to 1.1% (2009-2010).
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 183 (Book Page): [The survey showed the national ARTI was about 1.5 per cent. The second survey (2009-2010) shows that the national ARTI is 1.1 per cent.]

category: Analyze the local and global burden of Tuberculosis
front: Q: What are the specific global targets for DOTS implementation regarding cure and detection rates?
back:
- Cure rate: 85% of new smear-positive cases.
- Detection rate: 70% of new smear-positive cases.
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 183 (Book Page): [The target of DOTS programme is successful treatment or cure rate of 85 per cent of new smear positive cases, and detection of 70 per cent of such cases.]

category: Discuss prevention and control measures for Pulmonary TB in line with WHO strategies to control TB
front: What is the central public health strategy currently recommended by WHO for TB control?
back: The DOTS strategy (Directly Observed Treatment, Short-course), now a core part of the 'Stop TB Strategy'.
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 183 (Book Page): [DOTS remains central to the public health approach to tuberculosis control, which is now presented as Stop TB Strategy.]

category: Discuss prevention and control measures for Pulmonary TB in line with WHO strategies to control TB
front: Describe the physiological rationale for the 'Two-Phase' chemotherapy in TB control.
back:
1. Intensive Phase: Rapidly kills active bacilli to reduce infectivity.
2. Continuation Phase: Sterilizes 'persisters' (dormant bacilli) to prevent relapse.
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 194 (Book Page): [intensive phase... to kill off as many bacilli as possible... continuation phase is aimed at sterilizing the smaller number of dormant or persisting bacilli.]

category: Discuss prevention and control measures for Pulmonary TB in line with WHO strategies to control TB
front: Why is sputum microscopy preferred over X-ray as the primary case-finding tool in WHO strategies?
back: It is reliable, cost-effective, and specifically identifies 'sputum-positive' cases, who are the primary sources of community infection.
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 192 (Book Page): [Sputum smear examination by direct microscopy is now considered the method of choice... enables us to discover the epidemiologically most important cases.]

category: Discuss prevention and control measures for Pulmonary TB in line with WHO strategies to control TB
front: A child under 5 lives with a sputum-positive TB patient. What is the recommended preventive measure?
back: Chemoprophylaxis, typically using Isoniazid (INH) for 6-12 months, after ruling out active disease.
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 204 (Book Page): [Chemoprophylaxis (now termed preventive treatment) with INH for one year... has been tried in contact reactors.]

category: Discuss prevention and control measures for Pulmonary TB in line with WHO strategies to control TB
front: What are the five essential technical components of the WHO DOTS strategy?
back:
1. Political commitment
2. Quality-assured bacteriology
3. Standardized treatment with supervision
4. Uninterrupted drug supply
5. Systematic monitoring/evaluation.
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 208 (Book Page): [1. Pursuing high-quality DOTS expansion... Political commitment... bacteriology... Standardized treatment... drug supply... Monitoring and evaluation.]

category: Discuss prevention and control measures for Pulmonary TB in line with WHO strategies to control TB
front: What are the specific WHO global targets for TB case detection and treatment success?
back:
1. Detect 70% of new smear-positive cases.
2. Successfully treat (cure) 85% of detected cases.
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 183 (Book Page): [The target of DOTS programme is successful treatment or cure rate of 85 per cent of new smear positive cases, and detection of 70 per cent of such cases.]

category: Discuss prevention and control measures for Pulmonary TB in line with WHO strategies to control TB
front: How does BCG vaccination timing in India align with WHO EPI recommendations?
back: Administered 'very early' in infancy, ideally at birth or at 6 weeks (simultaneously with DPT/Polio).
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 203 (Book Page): [national policy is to administer BCG very early in infancy either at birth... or at 6 weeks of age simultaneously with other immunizing agents.]

category: Discuss prevention and control measures for Pulmonary TB in line with WHO strategies to control TB
front: Contrast the epidemiological impact of BCG vaccination versus Case-finding and Treatment.
back: Case-finding/Treatment reduces community transmission (pool of infection); BCG provides individual protection against severe childhood forms but has minimal impact on community-wide transmission.
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 204 (Book Page): [BCG vaccination is less effective in controlling tuberculosis as compared to active case-finding... it will not contribute significantly to the reduction in the overall risk of infection in the community.]

category: Discuss prevention and control measures for Pulmonary TB in line with WHO strategies to control TB
front: What are the 2015 'Stop TB' targets regarding TB prevalence and mortality?
back: Reduce global TB prevalence and death rates by 50% relative to 1990 levels.
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 206 (Book Page): [By 2015: The global burden of TB (prevalence and death rates) will be reduced by 50% relative to 1990 levels.]

category: Discuss prevention and control measures for Pulmonary TB in line with WHO strategies to control TB
front: What is the primary clinical benefit of BCG vaccination in pediatric populations?
back: Protection against severe, disseminated forms of the disease, specifically Tuberculous Meningitis and Miliary Tuberculosis.
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 204 (Book Page): [there is evidence that BCG plays a valuable role in preventing severe forms of childhood tuberculosis, viz meningitis and miliary tuberculosis.]

category: Discuss prevention and control measures for Pulmonary TB in line with WHO strategies to control TB
front: Q: What are the five technical components of the WHO DOTS strategy for TB control?
back: 1. Political commitment. 2. Quality-assured bacteriology/microscopy. 3. Standardized supervised treatment (DOT). 4. Effective drug supply. 5. Monitoring and evaluation system.
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 208 (Book Page): [1. Political commitment... 2. Case detection through quality-assured bacteriology... 3. Standardized treatment with supervision... 4. An effective drug supply... 5. Monitoring and evaluation system]

category: Discuss prevention and control measures for Pulmonary TB in line with WHO strategies to control TB
front: Q: What is the physiological rationale for the two-phase chemotherapy approach in WHO TB guidelines?
back: The intensive phase (1-3 months) kills rapidly multiplying bacilli. The continuation phase (6-9 months) targets dormant/persisting bacilli to ensure sterilization and prevent relapse.
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 193 (Book Page): [intensive phase... to kill off as many bacilli as possible... continuation phase is aimed at sterilizing the smaller number of dormant or persisting bacilli]

category: Discuss prevention and control measures for Pulmonary TB in line with WHO strategies to control TB
front: Q: Contrast sputum smear microscopy with other tools in WHO case-finding strategies.
back: Sputum microscopy is the 'method of choice' as it is cheap, reliable, and identifies the most infectious cases (pool of infection).
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 192 (Book Page): [Sputum smear examination... enables us to discover the epidemiologically most important cases... which contributes most of the new cases to the 'pool of infection']

category: Discuss prevention and control measures for Pulmonary TB in line with WHO strategies to control TB
front: Q: In a clinical scenario, how does Directly Observed Treatment (DOT) prevent the emergence of MDR-TB?
back: It ensures patient adherence (compliance) and an uninterrupted drug supply. This prevents treatment failure and the selection of drug-resistant bacterial strains.
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 183 (Book Page): [Prevents failure of treatment and the emergence of MDR-TB by ensuring patient adherence and uninterrupted drug supply]

category: Discuss prevention and control measures for Pulmonary TB in line with WHO strategies to control TB
front: Q: How did Rifampicin and Pyrazinamide change the pharmacological management of TB duration?
back: Their introduction allowed treatment to be reduced from the traditional 18 months to a 6-9 month short-course regimen by effectively sterilizing lesions.
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 194 (Book Page): [introduction of rifampicin or of pyrazinamide... made it possible to reduce the duration of treatment... reduced to 6-9 months]

category: Discuss prevention and control measures for Pulmonary TB in line with WHO strategies to control TB
front: Q: What are the WHO-defined targets for treatment success and case detection in DOTS?
back: The targets are a cure/success rate of 85% and a detection rate of 70% for new smear-positive cases.
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 183 (Book Page): [The target of DOTS programme is successful treatment or cure rate of 85 per cent of new smear positive cases, and detection of 70 per cent of such cases.]

category: Discuss prevention and control measures for Pulmonary TB in line with WHO strategies to control TB
front: Q: How is the 'continuation phase' of TB treatment monitored for patient compliance under WHO strategy?
back: The patient uses a multiblister combipack. The first dose is supervised; the rest is verified by the return of empty blister packs.
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 202 (Book Page): [consumption of medicine in the continuation phase is also checked by return of empty multiblister combipack]

category: Discuss prevention and control measures for Pulmonary TB in line with WHO strategies to control TB
front: Q: Which specific severe childhood complications does BCG vaccination aim to prevent in high-burden regions?
back: BCG provides a high level of protection against childhood Tuberculous Meningitis and Disseminated (Miliary) Tuberculosis.
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 203 (Book Page): [BCG... provides a high level of protection, particularly against the severe forms of childhood tuberculosis and tuberculous meningitis.]

category: Discuss prevention and control measures for Pulmonary TB in line with WHO strategies to control TB
front: Q: How does the WHO Stop TB strategy address the metabolic synergy between HIV and Tuberculosis?
back: It implements collaborative TB/HIV activities and ensures high-quality DOTS expansion for vulnerable co-infected populations to reduce incidence.
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 208 (Book Page): [Addressing TB/HIV, MDR-TB and other challenges — Implement collaborative TB/HIV activities]

category: Discuss prevention and control measures for Pulmonary TB in line with WHO strategies to control TB
front: Q: What is the significance of the 'Danish 1331' strain in WHO TB control programs?
back: It is the specific WHO-recommended strain used for the production of the live-attenuated BCG vaccine to ensure quality control.
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 202 (Book Page): [The WHO has recommended the “Danish 1331” strain for the production of BCG vaccine.]

category: Discuss prevention and control measures for Pulmonary TB in line with WHO strategies to control TB
front: Q: What are the two fundamental components of a National Tuberculosis Programme?
back:
1. Case-finding (curative component)
2. Treatment (using chemotherapy)
3. BCG vaccination (preventive component)
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 188 (Book Page): [The control measures consist of a curative component — namely case finding and treatment; and a preventive component — namely BCG vaccination. These are the two fundamental components of a national tuberculosis programme.]

category: Discuss prevention and control measures for Pulmonary TB in line with WHO strategies to control TB
front: Q: Describe the two-phase chemotherapy strategy for Pulmonary TB.
back:
1. Intensive phase (1–3 months): Uses 3+ drugs to kill rapidly multiplying bacilli.
2. Continuation phase: Sterilizes remaining dormant/persisting bacilli over 6–9 months.
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 193 (Book Page): [(i) the first is a short, aggressive or intense phase... lasting 1-3 months... (ii) the second or “continuation” phase is aimed at sterilizing the smaller number of dormant or persisting bacilli.]

category: Discuss prevention and control measures for Pulmonary TB in line with WHO strategies to control TB
front: Q: Contrast Domiciliary treatment with Hospitalization according to the Chennai Study.
back: Domiciliary treatment (home-based) is equally effective, cheaper, and preferred over sanatorium care for TB control.
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 193 (Book Page): [hospital treatment has no advantage over domiciliary treatment, and domiciliary treatment is to be preferred because in the long run, it is so much cheaper...]

category: Discuss prevention and control measures for Pulmonary TB in line with WHO strategies to control TB
front: Q: How does the Stop TB Strategy address the challenge of MDR-TB and HIV co-infection?
back:
1. Implementation of collaborative TB/HIV activities.
2. Prevention and control of Multi-Drug Resistant (MDR) TB via high-quality DOTS expansion.
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 206 (Book Page): [Addressing TB/HIV, MDR-TB and other challenges — Implement collaborative TB/HIV activities — Prevent and control MDR-TB]

category: Discuss prevention and control measures for Pulmonary TB in line with WHO strategies to control TB
front: Q: What are the five technical components of the WHO DOTS strategy?
back:
1. Political commitment
2. Quality-assured bacteriology (Microscopy)
3. Standardized treatment/supervision
4. Uninterrupted drug supply
5. Monitoring and evaluation system
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 206 (Book Page): [Pursuing high-quality DOTS expansion and enhancement a. Political commitment... b. Case detection through quality-assured bacteriology c. Standardized treatment... d. An effective drug supply... e. Monitoring and evaluation system]

category: Discuss prevention and control measures for Pulmonary TB in line with WHO strategies to control TB
front: Q: What is the preferred gold-standard tool for TB case-finding globally?
back: Sputum smear examination by direct microscopy; it is reliable, cheap, and identifies the most infectious cases.
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 188 (Book Page): [Sputum smear examination by direct microscopy is now considered the method of choice... It enables us to discover the epidemiologically most important cases...]

category: Discuss prevention and control measures for Pulmonary TB in line with WHO strategies to control TB
front: Q: Why is the birth dose of BCG prioritized in high-prevalence countries like Pakistan?
back: It provides high protection against severe childhood forms: Tuberculous meningitis and miliary tuberculosis.
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 203 (Book Page): [BCG administered early in life provides a high level of protection, particularly against the severe forms of childhood tuberculosis and tuberculous meningitis.]

category: Discuss prevention and control measures for Pulmonary TB in line with WHO strategies to control TB
front: Q: Define the 'Stop TB Partnership' targets for TB prevalence and death rates by 2015.
back: Reduce both global TB prevalence and death rates by 50% relative to 1990 levels.
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 206 (Book Page): [By 2015: The global burden of TB (prevalence and death rates) will be reduced by 50% relative to 1990 levels.]

category: Discuss prevention and control measures for Pulmonary TB in line with WHO strategies to control TB
front: Q: Describe the supervision mechanism during the Intensive Phase of DOTS.
back: A health worker or trained person directly watches the patient swallow every dose of medicine to ensure compliance.
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 194 (Book Page): [In DOTS, during the intensive phase of treatment a health worker or other trained person watches as the patient swallows the drug in his presence.]

category: Discuss prevention and control measures for Pulmonary TB in line with WHO strategies to control TB
front: Q: What is the criteria for 'DOTS coverage' in a national administrative unit?
back: Official adoption of the strategy and implementation of all four technical components of DOTS in the area.
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 182 (Book Page): [To be classified as DOTS, a country must have officially accepted and adopted the strategy... and must have implemented the four technical components of DOTS...]

category: Discuss prevention and control measures for Pulmonary TB in line with WHO strategies to control TB
front: What is the primary high-yield method for TB case detection in WHO strategies?
back: Sputive smear examination by direct microscopy (Gold Standard for finding infectors).
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 188 (Book Page): [Sputum smear examination by direct microscopy is now considered the method of choice.]

category: Discuss prevention and control measures for Pulmonary TB in line with WHO strategies to control TB
front: Explain the purpose of the 'Intensive Phase' in TB chemotherapy.
back: To kill rapidly multiplying bacilli initially, preventing the emergence of 'persisters' and reducing relapse risk.
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 193 (Book Page): [During this intensive phase, three or more drugs are combined to kill off as many bacilli as possible... the less likely are “persisters” to emerge.]

category: Discuss prevention and control measures for Pulmonary TB in line with WHO strategies to control TB
front: Contrast the infectious hazard of Smear-Positive vs. Smear-Negative Pulmonary TB.
back: Smear-Positive: Highly infectious (10-15 contacts/year). Smear-Negative: Minimal hazard for transmission.
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 187 (Book Page): [Patients with infectious pulmonary tuberculosis disease can infect 10-15 persons in a year... Patients with extrapulmonary tuberculosis or smear-negative tuberculosis constitute a minimal hazard for transmission.]

category: Discuss prevention and control measures for Pulmonary TB in line with WHO strategies to control TB
front: A 4-year-old child is a close household contact of a smear-positive TB case. Management?
back: Chemoprophylaxis with Isoniazid (INH) for 6-12 months (after ruling out active TB).
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 204 (Book Page): [Chemoprophylaxis (now termed preventive treatment) with INH for one year... has been tried in contact reactors.]

category: Discuss prevention and control measures for Pulmonary TB in line with WHO strategies to control TB
front: List the four standard drugs used in the intensive phase of Short-Course Chemotherapy.
back: Isoniazid (H), Rifampicin (R), Pyrazinamide (Z), and Ethambutol (E) or Streptomycin (S).
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 194 (Book Page): [initial intensive phase with 4 drugs (INH, rifampicin and pyrazinamide, supplemented by either streptomycin or ethambutol).]

category: Discuss prevention and control measures for Pulmonary TB in line with WHO strategies to control TB
front: State the two key performance targets for a successful WHO DOTS programme.
back: 1. Cure Rate: 85% of new smear-positive cases. 2. Case Detection: 70% of such cases.
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 183 (Book Page): [The target of DOTS programme is successful treatment or cure rate of 85 per cent of new smear positive cases, and detection of 70 per cent of such cases.]

category: Discuss prevention and control measures for Pulmonary TB in line with WHO strategies to control TB
front: What are the two fundamental components of a National TB Control Programme?
back: 1. Curative: Case-finding and treatment. 2. Preventive: BCG vaccination.
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 188 (Book Page): [The control measures consist of a curative component — namely case finding and treatment; and a preventive component — namely BCG vaccination.]

category: Discuss prevention and control measures for Pulmonary TB in line with WHO strategies to control TB
front: Differentiate the role of BCG vs. Case Finding in controlling community transmission.
back: BCG: Prevents severe childhood forms (meningitis) but limited community impact. Case Finding/Treatment: Primary tool for reducing community transmission risk.
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 203 (Book Page): [BCG vaccination is less effective in controlling tuberculosis as compared to active case-finding and chemotherapy... it will not contribute significantly to the reduction in the overall risk of infection.]

category: Discuss prevention and control measures for Pulmonary TB in line with WHO strategies to control TB
front: How does the 'Directly Observed' component of DOTS prevent Multi-Drug Resistance (MDR)?
back: By ensuring patient adherence and swallowing of drugs, preventing treatment failure and the selection of resistant strains.
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 183 (Book Page): [Prevents failure of treatment and the emergence of MDR-TB by ensuring patient adherence and uninterrupted drug supply.]

category: Discuss prevention and control measures for Pulmonary TB in line with WHO strategies to control TB
front: Identify the WHO-recommended vaccine strain for BCG production.
back: Danish 1331 strain.
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 202 (Book Page): [The WHO has recommended the “Danish 1331” strain for the production of BCG vaccine.]

category: Discuss prevention and control measures for Pulmonary TB in line with WHO strategies to control TB
front: Q: List the five technical components of the WHO DOTS strategy for TB control.
back:
1. Political commitment
2. Quality-assured microscopy
3. Standardized supervised treatment (DOT)
4. Uninterrupted drug supply
5. Systematic monitoring/evaluation.
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 183 (Book Page): [The four technical components of DOTS... Political commitment... Case detection through quality-assured bacteriology... Standardized treatment with supervision... effective drug supply... Monitoring and evaluation system.]

category: Discuss prevention and control measures for Pulmonary TB in line with WHO strategies to control TB
front: Q: Distinguish the objectives of the Intensive vs. Continuation phases in TB chemotherapy.
back:
• Intensive (1–3 months): Kills fast-multiplying bacilli; prevents resistance.
• Continuation (4–6 months): Sterilizes dormant/persisting bacilli; prevents relapse.
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 194 (Book Page): [intensive phase... to kill off as many bacilli as possible... continuation phase is aimed at sterilizing the smaller number of dormant or persisting bacilli.]

category: Discuss prevention and control measures for Pulmonary TB in line with WHO strategies to control TB
front: Q: Why is sputum microscopy prioritized over Chest X-ray in WHO case-finding strategies?
back:
• Most reliable and cost-effective tool.
• Identifies the 'infectious pool' (smear-positive cases).
• High specificity for diagnosing public health threats.
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 188 (Book Page): [Sputum smear examination by direct microscopy is now considered the method of choice... It enables us to discover the epidemiologically most important cases.]

category: Discuss prevention and control measures for Pulmonary TB in line with WHO strategies to control TB
front: Q: What defines a 'missed case' in the global TB burden according to WHO?
back:
Cases that are either:
1. Not diagnosed.
2. Diagnosed but not reported to the National TB Program/WHO.
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 183 (Book Page): [About 3 million missed cases were either not diagnosed or diagnosed but not reported.]

category: Discuss prevention and control measures for Pulmonary TB in line with WHO strategies to control TB
front: Q: Which two drugs allowed the reduction of TB treatment from 18 months to 6 months?
back:
• Rifampicin
• Pyrazinamide
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 194 (Book Page): [With the introduction of rifampicin and pyrazinamide, this period is now successfully reduced to 6-9 months.]

category: Discuss prevention and control measures for Pulmonary TB in line with WHO strategies to control TB
front: Q: State the global WHO targets for successful DOTS implementation.
back:
• Cure Rate: ≥85% of new smear-positive cases.
• Case Detection Rate: ≥70% of estimated new cases.
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 183 (Book Page): [The target of DOTS programme is successful treatment or cure rate of 85 per cent of new smear positive cases, and detection of 70 per cent of such cases.]

category: Discuss prevention and control measures for Pulmonary TB in line with WHO strategies to control TB
front: Q: What is the 'Chennai Study's' high-yield contribution to TB control strategy?
back: Established that domiciliary (home) treatment is as effective as sanatorium (hospital) treatment, without increasing contact risk.
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 194 (Book Page): [Chennai Study, that prompted a radical departure from the traditional sanatorium to ambulatory or domiciliary treatment.]

category: Discuss prevention and control measures for Pulmonary TB in line with WHO strategies to control TB
front: Q: How does WHO define a 'DOTS Area' in public health management?
back: A township, district, or administrative unit where health services have officially adopted and implemented all four technical DOTS components.
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 183 (Book Page): [DOTS coverage is defined as the percentage of the national population living in areas where health services have adopted DOTS... lowest administrative or management units.]

category: Discuss prevention and control measures for Pulmonary TB in line with WHO strategies to control TB
front: Q: Why is BCG vaccination given at birth in high-prevalence countries like Pakistan/India?
back: To protect against severe childhood forms (Tuberculous Meningitis and Miliary TB) before exposure to environmental mycobacteria occurs.
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 203 (Book Page): [BCG administered early in life provides a high level of protection, particularly against the severe forms of childhood tuberculosis and tuberculous meningitis.]

category: Discuss prevention and control measures for Pulmonary TB in line with WHO strategies to control TB
front: Q: State the WHO recommended BCG strain, dose, and administration site.
back:
• Strain: Danish 1331.
• Dose: 0.1 ml (0.05 ml for <1 month).
• Route/Site: Intradermal; Left Upper Arm.
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 202 (Book Page): [WHO has recommended the “Danish 1331” strain... 0.1 ml Intra-dermal Left Upper Arm (0.05 ml until 1 month age).]

category: Discuss prevention and control measures for Pulmonary TB in line with WHO strategies to control TB
front: What are the five essential technical components of the WHO DOTS strategy?
back:
• Political commitment with sustained financing
• Case detection by quality-assured sputum microscopy
• Standardized treatment with direct observation (DOT)
• Uninterrupted drug supply system
• Standardized recording and reporting system
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 208 (Book Page): [1. Pursuing high-quality DOTS expansion and enhancement: a. Political commitment... b. Case detection through quality-assured bacteriology c. Standardized treatment with supervision... d. An effective drug supply... e. Monitoring and evaluation system]

category: Discuss prevention and control measures for Pulmonary TB in line with WHO strategies to control TB
front: Explain the primary pathophysiological objective of the 'Intensive Phase' in TB chemotherapy.
back:
• Rapidly kill the bulk of actively multiplying bacilli
• Induce rapid sputum conversion to non-infectious state
• Prevent the emergence of 'persister' or dormant bacilli
• Minimize the risk of early relapse
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 194 (Book Page): [During this intensive phase, three or more drugs are combined to kill off as many bacilli as possible. The more rapidly the bacilli are killed initially, the less likely are “persisters” to emerge.]

category: Discuss prevention and control measures for Pulmonary TB in line with WHO strategies to control TB
front: Why is sputum smear microscopy prioritized over Chest X-ray in WHO case-finding strategies?
back:
• Reliability and cost-effectiveness
• Identifies 'smear-positive' cases (the primary pool of infection)
• More specific than X-ray for active TB
• Essential for monitoring treatment response
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 192 (Book Page): [The reliability, cheapness and ease of direct microscopic examination has made it number one case-finding method... It enables us to discover the epidemiologically most important cases... which contributes most... to the “pool of infection”.]

category: Discuss prevention and control measures for Pulmonary TB in line with WHO strategies to control TB
front: A child under 5 resides with a smear-positive TB patient. What is the recommended WHO preventive measure?
back:
• Isoniazid (INH) chemoprophylaxis for 6-12 months
• Screening for active disease first
• BCG vaccination if not already given
• Close clinical monitoring for breakthrough symptoms
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 204 (Book Page): [Chemoprophylaxis... with INH for one year... has been tried in contact reactors... BCG vaccination of uninfected individuals (usually children) can prevent tuberculosis in them.]

category: Discuss prevention and control measures for Pulmonary TB in line with WHO strategies to control TB
front: What are the two specific performance targets set by WHO for national DOTS programs?
back:
• Cure rate: Successful treatment of 85% of new smear-positive cases
• Detection rate: Identification of 70% of new smear-positive cases
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 183 (Book Page): [The target of DOTS programme is successful treatment or cure rate of 85 per cent of new smear positive cases, and detection of 70 per cent of such cases.]

category: Discuss prevention and control measures for Pulmonary TB in line with WHO strategies to control TB
front: List the six pillars of the WHO 'Stop TB Strategy'.
back:
1. Pursue high-quality DOTS expansion
2. Address TB/HIV and MDR-TB
3. Contribute to health system strengthening
4. Engage all care providers (PPM)
5. Empower people/communities
6. Enable/promote research
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 208 (Book Page): [Components of the strategy... 1. Pursuing high-quality DOTS... 2. Addressing TB/HIV, MDR-TB... 3. Contributing to health system strengthening 4. Engaging all care providers 5. Empowering people with TB... 6. Enabling and promoting research.]

category: Discuss prevention and control measures for Pulmonary TB in line with WHO strategies to control TB
front: How does the 'Continuation Phase' of Short-Course Chemotherapy differ in function from the 'Intensive Phase'?
back:
• Target: Eliminates dormant or 'persisting' bacilli
• Goal: Achieves complete sterilization of lesions to prevent relapse
• Duration: Typically 4-6 months using fewer drugs (e.g., INH/Rifampicin)
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 194 (Book Page): [the second or “continuation” phase is aimed at sterilizing the smaller number of dormant or persisting bacilli... now successfully reduced to 6-9 months.]

category: Discuss prevention and control measures for Pulmonary TB in line with WHO strategies to control TB
front: Regarding the Stop TB Strategy, what are 'Public-Private Mix' (PPM) approaches?
back:
• Engaging all care providers (private practitioners, NGOs)
• Implementation of International Standards for TB Care (ISTC)
• Linking private clinics to the national referral/reporting system
• Ensuring standardized treatment across all health sectors
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 208 (Book Page): [4. Engaging all care providers — Public-Public and Public-Private Mix (PPM) approaches — Implement international standards for tuberculosis care.]

category: Discuss prevention and control measures for Pulmonary TB in line with WHO strategies to control TB
front: Which specific forms of childhood TB are most effectively prevented by BCG vaccination?
back:
• Tuberculous Meningitis
• Miliary (Disseminated) Tuberculosis
• Note: Protection against adult pulmonary TB is highly variable (0-80%)
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 203 (Book Page): [BCG administered early in life provides a high level of protection, particularly against the severe forms of childhood tuberculosis and tuberculous meningitis.]

category: Discuss prevention and control measures for Pulmonary TB in line with WHO strategies to control TB
front: What are the requirements for a district to reach the status of 'Tuberculosis Control'?
back:
• Reduction in prevalence and incidence in the community
• Effective implementation of all DOTS components
• High rate of cure achieved in infectious (sputum+) cases
• Minimal treatment default/failure rates
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 188 (Book Page): [Tuberculosis control means reduction in the prevalence and incidence of disease... The most powerful weapon, however, is the combination of case-finding and treatment.]

category: Discuss prevention and control measures for Pulmonary TB in line with WHO strategies to control TB
front: What are the five technical components of the WHO DOTS strategy for Tuberculosis control?
back:
1. Political commitment
2. Quality-assured bacteriology (sputum microscopy)
3. Standardized treatment with supervision (DOT)
4. Effective drug supply
5. Monitoring and evaluation system
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 183 (Book Page): [To be classified as DOTS, a country must... have implemented the four technical components of DOTS... Political commitment... Case detection through quality-assured bacteriology... Standardized treatment... Effective drug supply... Monitoring and evaluation.]

category: Discuss prevention and control measures for Pulmonary TB in line with WHO strategies to control TB
front: Explain the pathophysiological roles of the intensive and continuation phases in TB chemotherapy.
back:
• Intensive phase (1-3 months): Combined drugs kill rapidly multiplying bacilli to prevent resistance.
• Continuation phase (4-6 months): Focuses on sterilizing 'persister' or dormant bacilli to prevent relapse.
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 193 (Book Page): [intensive phase... to kill off as many bacilli as possible... continuation phase is aimed at sterilizing the smaller number of dormant or persisting bacilli.]

category: Discuss prevention and control measures for Pulmonary TB in line with WHO strategies to control TB
front: Contrast the utility of sputum smear examination versus other tools for TB case-finding.
back:
• Sputum Smear: Method of choice; identifies the 'pool of infection' (infectious cases).
• Chest X-ray/Other: Higher sensitivity but less specific for identifying community infectors.
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 188 (Book Page): [Sputum smear examination by direct microscopy is now considered the method of choice. It enables us to discover the epidemiologically most important cases... which contributes most... to the pool of infection.]

category: Discuss prevention and control measures for Pulmonary TB in line with WHO strategies to control TB
front: Why might a region with high BCG coverage still show high adult TB incidence?
back:
• BCG protects children against severe forms (meningitis/miliary).
• It provides partial/variable protection (0-80%) against pulmonary TB.
• Minimal impact on reducing the overall community risk of infection.
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 203 (Book Page): [BCG vaccination... can have only a relatively small epidemiological effect in that it will not contribute significantly to the reduction in the overall risk of infection in the community.]

category: Discuss prevention and control measures for Pulmonary TB in line with WHO strategies to control TB
front: What is the pharmacological rationale for adding Pyrazinamide or Rifampicin to the intensive phase?
back:
• They reduce treatment duration from 18 to 6-9 months.
• They effectively target dormant 'persisters'.
• They prevent the emergence of drug-resistant strains.
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 194 (Book Page): [the addition of rifampicin or of pyrazinamide... made it possible to reduce the duration of treatment... to 6-9 months... and a reduction in the frequency of emergence of drug-resistant bacilli.]

category: Discuss prevention and control measures for Pulmonary TB in line with WHO strategies to control TB
front: What are the specific WHO targets for DOTS cure and case detection rates?
back:
• Cure/Treatment Success Rate: 85% of new smear-positive cases.
• Case Detection Rate: 70% of new smear-positive cases.
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 183 (Book Page): [The target of DOTS programme is successful treatment or cure rate of 85 per cent of new smear positive cases, and detection of 70 per cent of such cases.]

category: Discuss prevention and control measures for Pulmonary TB in line with WHO strategies to control TB
front: Applying the 'Chennai Study' findings, why is domiciliary treatment preferred over sanatorium care?
back:
• Infectivity: No higher risk to contacts at home.
• Economic: Significantly cheaper for the health system.
• Social: Uses existing primary health care structures without isolation stigma.
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 193 (Book Page): [incidence of tuberculosis was no greater in the contacts of patients treated at home than in the contacts of patients treated in sanatoria... domiciliary treatment is to be preferred because... it is so much cheaper.]

category: Discuss prevention and control measures for Pulmonary TB in line with WHO strategies to control TB
front: Differentiate the infection potential of pulmonary versus extra-pulmonary TB cases.
back:
• Pulmonary (Smear-positive): Major source of droplet nuclei; highly infectious.
• Extra-pulmonary/Smear-negative: Minimal hazard for transmission to the community.
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 188 (Book Page): [Tuberculosis is transmitted mainly by droplet infection... generated by sputum-positive patients... Patients with extrapulmonary tuberculosis or smear-negative tuberculosis constitute a minimal hazard.]

category: Discuss prevention and control measures for Pulmonary TB in line with WHO strategies to control TB
front: Describe the loop of TB transmission and the influence of 'persister' bacilli on relapse.
back:
• One infectious case infects 10-15 people annually.
• 'Persisters' remain dormant during treatment.
• If not eliminated during continuation phase, they resume multiplication, causing clinical relapse.
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 187 (Book Page): [The slow multipliers are the source of persister or dormant bacilli... when conditions are favourable they may start multiplying again and cause active disease... they are the seeds of a future relapse.]

category: Discuss prevention and control measures for Pulmonary TB in line with WHO strategies to control TB
front: What are the primary target diseases for reduction under the WHO 'Stop TB Partnership' targets?
back:
• Reduce prevalence and death rates by 50% relative to 1990 levels.
• Target 2050: Incidence less than 1 case per million per year.
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 206 (Book Page): [By 2015: The global burden of TB (prevalence and death rates) will be reduced by 50% relative to 1990 levels... By 2050: The global incidence... less than or equal to 1 case per million population.]

category: Explain significance of TB DOTS therapy for TB control
front: Q: What does the acronym DOTS stand for in the context of Tuberculosis control?
back: Directly Observed Treatment, Short-course.
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 194 (Book Page): [Directly Observed Treatment, Short Course (DOTS) Chemotherapy]

category: Explain significance of TB DOTS therapy for TB control
front: Q: How does DOTS therapy specifically prevent the emergence of Multi-Drug Resistant TB (MDR-TB)?
back: Ensures patient adherence through direct supervision; maintains an uninterrupted drug supply; prevents treatment failure.
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 183 (Book Page): [Prevents failure of treatment and the emergence of MDR-TB by ensuring patient adherence and uninterrupted drug supply]

category: Explain significance of TB DOTS therapy for TB control
front: Q: What is the significance of DOTS regarding the accuracy of Tuberculosis diagnosis?
back: Implementation of DOTS more than doubles the accuracy of TB diagnosis compared to traditional methods.
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 183 (Book Page): [Accuracy of TB diagnosis is more than doubled]

category: Explain significance of TB DOTS therapy for TB control
front: Q: In a resource-poor setting, how does DOTS ensure patient compliance during the continuation phase?
back: Issue of weekly multiblister combipacks; first dose swallowed under supervision; checking empty packs upon return for the next supply.
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 194 (Book Page): [During continuation phase, the patient is issued medicine for one week in a multiblister combipack... consumption... is also checked by return of empty multiblister combipack]

category: Explain significance of TB DOTS therapy for TB control
front: Q: What is the primary role of the health worker during the intensive phase of DOTS?
back: To physically watch and confirm that the patient swallows every dose of the prescribed medication.
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 194 (Book Page): [During the intensive phase of treatment a health worker or other trained person watches as the patient swallows the drug in his presence.]

category: Explain significance of TB DOTS therapy for TB control
front: Q: What are the two primary global performance targets for a successful DOTS programme?
back: Cure rate: 85% of new smear-positive cases; Case detection: 70% of new smear-positive cases.
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 183 (Book Page): [The target of DOTS programme is successful treatment or cure rate of 85 per cent of new smear positive cases, and detection of 70 per cent of such cases.]

category: Explain significance of TB DOTS therapy for TB control
front: Q: Why is DOTS considered superior to self-administered treatment for community TB control?
back: Prevents the spread of infection by achieving high cure rates (up to 95%) and reducing the community pool of infectors.
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 183 (Book Page): [Prevents the spread of the tuberculosis infection, thus reducing the incidence and prevalence of tuberculosis; Treatment success rate is upto 95 per cent]

category: Explain significance of TB DOTS therapy for TB control
front: Q: A patient develops TB relapse. How does the DOTS strategy differentiate its management from a new case?
back: Relapse cases are classified as Category II, requiring a different standardized treatment regimen and duration compared to new cases (Category I).
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 194 (Book Page): [The cases are divided into two types of categories — category I and category II. Table 3 shows the type of cases included in each kind of category]

category: Explain significance of TB DOTS therapy for TB control
front: Q: What is the significance of the continuation phase in the two-phase DOTS chemotherapy?
back: Aims at sterilization; eliminates smaller numbers of dormant or persisting bacilli to prevent future relapse.
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 193 (Book Page): [The second or “continuation” phase is aimed at sterilizing the smaller number of dormant or persisting bacilli.]

category: Explain significance of TB DOTS therapy for TB control
front: Q: What is the method of choice for case-finding within the DOTS framework?
back: Sputum smear examination by direct microscopy.
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 192 (Book Page): [Sputum smear examination by direct microscopy is now considered the method of choice... enabled us to discover the epidemiologically most important cases]

category: Explain significance of TB DOTS therapy for TB control
front: Q: What is the core public health strategy recommended by WHO for effective TB control?
back: DOTS (Directly Observed Treatment, Short Course), which is the central component of the global 'Stop TB Strategy'.
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 183 (Book Page): [DOTS remains central to the public health approach to tuberculosis control, which is now presented as Stop TB Strategy.]

category: Explain significance of TB DOTS therapy for TB control
front: Q: How does DOTS therapy specifically prevent the development of Multi-Drug Resistant TB (MDR-TB)?
back: It ensures strict patient adherence and an uninterrupted drug supply, preventing treatment failure and the emergence of resistant strains.
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 183 (Book Page): [Prevents failure of treatment and the emergence of MDR-TB by ensuring patient adherence and uninterrupted drug supply.]

category: Explain significance of TB DOTS therapy for TB control
front: Q: Contrast the supervision requirements between the intensive and continuation phases of DOTS.
back:
• Intensive: Health worker watches every dose swallowed.
• Continuation: Worker watches first weekly dose; empty multiblister packs are checked later.
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 194 (Book Page): [During the intensive phase... a health worker... watches as the patient swallows the drug... During continuation phase... the first dose is swallowed... in the presence of health worker.]

category: Explain significance of TB DOTS therapy for TB control
front: Q: A patient feels better after 2 months and wants to stop. Why is supervision critical now?
back: To ensure the 'continuation phase' is completed, which is essential for sterilizing dormant 'persister' bacilli and preventing relapse.
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 193 (Book Page): [the second or “continuation” phase is aimed at sterilizing the smaller number of dormant or persisting bacilli.]

category: Explain significance of TB DOTS therapy for TB control
front: Q: What pharmacological tool is used in the DOTS continuation phase to monitor adherence?
back: Weekly multiblister combipacks; adherence is verified by the return of the empty pack to the health worker.
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 194 (Book Page): [The consumption of medicine in the continuation phase is also checked by return of empty multiblister combipack.]

category: Explain significance of TB DOTS therapy for TB control
front: Q: What are the two primary numerical targets for a successful DOTS program?
back:
• Cure Rate: 85% of new smear-positive cases.
• Case Detection: 70% of estimated smear-positive cases.
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 183 (Book Page): [The target of DOTS programme is successful treatment or cure rate of 85 per cent of new smear positive cases, and detection of 70 per cent of such cases.]

category: Explain significance of TB DOTS therapy for TB control
front: Q: How does the DOTS strategy contribute to alleviating poverty within a community?
back: By saving lives, reducing the duration of illness (morbidity), and preventing the spread of infection to others.
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 183 (Book Page): [Helps alleviate poverty by saving lives, reducing duration of illness and preventing spread of infection.]

category: Explain significance of TB DOTS therapy for TB control
front: Q: Why is DOTS bacteriological conversion superior to clinical improvement as a measure of success?
back: Clinical improvement occurs early, but bacteriological conversion confirms the elimination of the infectious pool and treatment efficacy.
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 193 (Book Page): [The effects of chemotherapy are judged not by the anatomic healing of lesions, but mainly by the elimination of bacilli from the patient’s sputum.]

category: Explain significance of TB DOTS therapy for TB control
front: Q: What is the primary role of combining multiple drugs in the intensive phase of DOTS?
back: To kill rapidly multiplying bacilli quickly, minimizing the emergence of resistant 'persisters' and reducing the risk of relapse.
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 193 (Book Page): [During this intensive phase, three or more drugs are combined to kill off as many bacilli as possible... less likely are “persisters” to emerge.]

category: Explain significance of TB DOTS therapy for TB control
front: Q: List three technical components required to classify a program as a 'High-Quality DOTS' expansion.
back:
1. Political commitment.
2. Quality-assured bacteriology.
3. Standardized treatment with supervision.
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 206 (Book Page): [1. Pursuing high-quality DOTS expansion... a. Political commitment... b. Case detection through quality-assured bacteriology... c. Standardized treatment with supervision.]

category: Discuss prevention and control measures for Pulmonary TB in line with WHO strategies to control TB
front: What are the two fundamental components of a National Tuberculosis Control Programme?
back:
- Curative component: Case-finding and treatment
- Preventive component: BCG vaccination
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 188 (Book Page): [The control measures consist of a curative component — namely case finding and treatment; and a preventive component — namely BCG vaccination.]

category: Discuss prevention and control measures for Pulmonary TB in line with WHO strategies to control TB
front: Explain the biological rationale behind the two-phase chemotherapy strategy in TB control.
back:
- Intensive Phase: Kills rapidly multiplying bacilli to prevent drug resistance.
- Continuation Phase: Sterilizes dormant/persisting bacilli to prevent future relapse.
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 193 (Book Page): [first is a short, aggressive or intense phase... to kill off as many bacilli as possible... continuation phase is aimed at sterilizing the smaller number of dormant or persisting bacilli.]

category: Discuss prevention and control measures for Pulmonary TB in line with WHO strategies to control TB
front: Contrast the efficiency of 'Sputum Smear' vs 'Mass Screening' in case-finding.
back:
- Sputum Smear: Target choice; identifies the 'pool of infectors' effectively.
- Mass Screening: Less efficient; symptomatic individuals are the most 'fertile group' for detection.
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 188 (Book Page): [Sputum smear examination by direct microscopy is now considered the method of choice... enables us to discover the epidemiologically most important cases.]

category: Discuss prevention and control measures for Pulmonary TB in line with WHO strategies to control TB
front: In WHO's Stop TB Strategy, what are the primary targets for case detection and cure?
back:
- Cure Rate: 85% of new smear-positive cases.
- Case Detection: 70% of new smear-positive cases.
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 183 (Book Page): [The target of DOTS programme is successful treatment or cure rate of 85 per cent of new smear positive cases, and detection of 70 per cent of such cases.]

category: Discuss prevention and control measures for Pulmonary TB in line with WHO strategies to control TB
front: How does the continuation phase under DOTS chemotherapy ensure patient compliance?
back:
- Multi-blister packs issued weekly.
- Supervision: First dose of each pack swallowed in presence of a health worker.
- Accountability: Return of empty blister packs required for refill.
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 194 (Book Page): [In continuation phase, the patient is issued medicine for one week in a multiblister combipack, of which the first dose is swallowed by the patient in the presence of health worker... checked by return of empty multiblister combipack.]

category: Discuss prevention and control measures for Pulmonary TB in line with WHO strategies to control TB
front: What is the primary diagnostic criterion for identifying 'infectors' in the community?
back:
- Sputum Smear Positive for tubercle bacilli.
- These cases are the main contributors to the 'pool of infection.'
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 188 (Book Page): [discover the epidemiologically most important cases... i.e., those excreting tubercle bacilli in their sputum. This is the group which contributes most of the new cases to the ‘pool of infection’.]

category: Discuss prevention and control measures for Pulmonary TB in line with WHO strategies to control TB
front: Why is BCG vaccination considered limited in reducing the overall community risk of TB?
back:
- Protects individuals against severe childhood forms (meningitis/miliary TB).
- Minimal effect on community transmission as it does not eliminate the adult pool of infectors.
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 203 (Book Page): [BCG vaccination... will not contribute significantly to the reduction in the overall risk of infection in the community as a whole.]

category: Discuss prevention and control measures for Pulmonary TB in line with WHO strategies to control TB
front: Compare Domiciliary Treatment vs Hospitalization outcomes according to the Chennai Study.
back:
- No advantage in hospitalization over home treatment.
- Infection risk to contacts was equal in both settings.
- Domiciliary care is preferred for cost-efficiency and PHC management.
citation: In book "Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine", Page 194 (Book Page): [the Chennai Study, showed that the incidence of tuberculosis was no greater in the contacts of patients treated at home than in the contacts of patients treated in sanatoria.]

category: Discuss prevention and control measures for Pulmonary TB in line with WHO strategies to control TB
front: What bacterial metabolic trait requires Short-Course Chemotherapy (SCC) to include Rifampicin/Pyrazinamide?
back:
- Bacterial 'Persisters' (slow/dormant multipliers).
- These drugs reduce treatment from 18 months to 6–9 months by sterilizing these lesions.
